A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same survey, with readable main text, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–B. Renamed benchmarks and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 provides a literature synthesis and categorical mapping of published evaluation tools, not an original empirical study. Experimental findings and appendix task examples are attributed to cited works.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. AssistedDS and WebDS are reviewed as other researchers' work; no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical dataset analyses are reported.

M1.justification: The framework based on data-science activities, autonomy, and technological transformation is retained. Neither version introduces a proposed algorithm or model; the Tapilot-Crossing-to-CoTa rename does not change its described procedure.

E1.justification: AssistedDS and WebDS expand the literature reviewed, but are not datasets or tasks newly used for training or evaluation by this work. Neither version conducts its own benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed system against baselines. Newly cited benchmarks are survey subjects, and CoTa matches the previously discussed Tapilot-Crossing.

E3.justification: No author-conducted evaluation protocol is introduced or revised. The added benchmark descriptions summarize external protocols, while explanations of retained benchmarks do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: No original ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added. Appendix B retains the same six attributed task examples; WebDS's validation studies are only described as prior work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports original repeated-run statistics, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The new reference to WebDS stability analysis does not introduce statistical reporting for this survey.

E6.justification: The descriptive survey findings expand through new activity-coverage classifications for AssistedDS and WebDS in Tables 2–3. Existing classifications and cited performance values remain unchanged; these additions are qualitative literature mappings, not new model-performance measurements.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. Appendix A's activity definitions are unchanged, and the added taxonomy diagram illustrates the existing framework.

C1.justification: The abstract's three central findings are retained. The introduction makes the exclusion of model-performance analysis explicit and sharpens the substitution claim from evaluations 'often' making this assumption to 'more than half' doing so.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about simulated users oversimplifying real interactions and omitting domain experts. It also discusses blurred activity boundaries, recommends human-centered measures such as perceived helpfulness, and proposes cross-activity performance correlations once evaluation gaps are addressed.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data access provisions for this work are added. Local clarifications of published benchmark descriptions and updated publication links do not establish changed reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds AssistedDS, WebDS, Chintakunta et al.'s mapping study, and work by Haupt and Brynjolfsson and by Reiter. Section 2.4 explains how this survey complements the mapping study; the overall positioning remains intact. The CoTa citation updates an already covered work.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, and future directions receive localized expansions and clarifications, while the section and appendix organization is retained. v2 also renames Tapilot-Crossing, corrects the incomplete DiscoveryBench description, and removes the acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adds a reproduced taxonomy diagram as Figure 1 in Appendix A and one row each to Tables 2–3. The six existing appendix figures are preserved as Figures 2–7, with corresponding caption references and page reflow; the general visual design is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added literature, clearer survey scope, taxonomy illustration, and more specific discussion of human–AI evaluation modestly improve the survey's usefulness. Its central framework and conclusions remain stable. Removing the funding acknowledgments is a small loss of transparency, but the substantive additions support a limited net improvement.
